reading.body:
Microsoft/LinkedIn's listed product is LinkedIn Recruiter AI, categorized under hr & talent ai, with talent acquisition AI as the function this data names first.

The data also tags LinkedIn Recruiter AI with candidate matching, description of what the product does rather than how well it does it. Beyond that, the entry flags bias risk in hiring and GDPR for EU candidates, governance and dependency notes rather than technical specifications.

Microsoft/LinkedIn sits at the application layer here, a product built on top of underlying compute rather than a claim on the compute itself, so this entry does not speak to the buildings or power behind it. Beyond the category, the product name, and this short list of tags tied to linkedin.com, the data carries no user counts, revenue, funding, or headcount, so nothing here supports a claim about Microsoft/LinkedIn's scale or trajectory.

profile_text.body:
Microsoft/LinkedIn's website, linkedin.com, describes the service as a professional network with 1 billion members. The site says users can manage their professional identity, build and engage with their professional network, and access knowledge, insights and opportunities. Its pages list job categories such as engineering, business development, finance, and human resources, and software categories including recruiting software, sales intelligence software, and human resources management systems.

LinkedIn Recruiter AI is listed as a product in the HR and Talent AI category. It is a talent acquisition AI tool with candidate matching. The product note identifies bias risk in hiring and GDPR considerations for EU candidates.
